fixes.explanation: The LORD says, "…they will come over in chains and bow down to you." So bowing down is what the verse says they do. They trudge behind, and I bet that's a long walk. Then they confess that God is with you.

Nothing in this verse has them demanding a ransom, friend. The LORD says, "…they will come over in chains and bow down to you." After that, they confess that God is with you. Bowing down is what the verse gives.
The verse only has them heading one way. They "…will come over to you…" and "…trudge behind you…" Nothing in the verse has them turning back. The LORD says they bow down.
The verse says, "the makers of idols will depart together in disgrace." Together is the word the text uses, friend. It comes right after the line that they will all be put to shame and humiliated.
The verse says the opposite. It says, "They will all be put to shame and humiliated…" Then it says the makers of idols will depart together in disgrace. No medals handed out at this exit.
The verse doesn't mention new idols, friend. It says the makers of idols "…will depart together in disgrace." That's how the verse describes their leaving.

The verse says, "you will not be put to shame or humiliated, to ages everlasting." In the verse before, the makers of idols depart in disgrace, but Israel's story is different. Israel will be saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation. That's a long time to be safe, friend.

Close, since the verse before it does have people leaving. But this verse doesn't mention flight, friend. It says Israel will be saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation, and that "you will not be put to shame or humiliated…" So the word that fits the blank is shame.

No swords turn up anywhere in this verse, friend. It says Israel will be saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation. Then it says, "you will not be put to shame or humiliated…" The word that fits the blank is shame.

The verse says of the LORD that "He did not create it to be empty, but formed it to be inhabited." The earth was made to have people living on it. Then the LORD speaks: "I am the LORD, and there is no other."
No kings in this verse, friend. It says, "He did not create it to be empty, but formed it to be inhabited." Kings aren't the reason it gives. The earth was formed so that it would be lived in.

The LORD says, "Ignorant are those who carry idols of wood and pray to a god that cannot save." Those are the people He calls ignorant, friend. The verse says two things about them: they carry idols of wood, and they pray to a god that cannot save.

The idol makers don't get any credit here. Earlier in this passage, the makers of idols depart together in disgrace. When the LORD asks who foretold this, He answers, "Was it not I, the LORD?" The credit goes to Him alone.
The LORD says, "Surely they will say of Me, 'In the LORD alone are righteousness and strength.'" The word "alone" is doing the heavy lifting. That's what He says they will say of Him.
The verse goes the other way, friend. It says that in the LORD, all descendants of Israel "will be justified and will exult." The verse says exult, not mourn. The word that fits the blank is exult.
The verse doesn't mention wandering, friend. It says that in the LORD all descendants of Israel "will be justified and will exult." So the word that fits the blank is exult.
